chunks: And as for what Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id narrated from Safwan ibn Yahya from Ishaq ibn 'Ammar from Abu Ibrahim (peace be upon him) who said:

I asked him about a man who had a female slave and he married her to another man. [I asked]: With whom is her divorce? He said: With her master. And that is because he married her while knowing that it was so. This report also carries what we previously mentioned, that by his saying 'with him is her divorce,' he meant 'her sale.' Thus, her sale is like the divorce. And it is permissible that the word 'divorce' be used metaphorically for that, because it is a cause of separation, just as divorce is so.
ai.seo_question: Who has the right to divorce a female slave married to a free man according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In this narration from *al-Istibsar*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that the master holds the right of *taliq* (divorce) for a female slave married to a free man, as he is the one who contracted the marriage. The text elucidates that the term 'divorce' is used metaphorically for 'sale' (*bay'*), since both acts serve as the legal cause for separation, reflecting the nuanced juristic reasoning of the Imams regarding mixed-status marriages.
